p1_tiger_fit_similarity.note: distance from modern TIGER road points to nearest Warren ink pixel (capped 15 px at half scale); fitted data, so optimistic; roads also moved since 1863

p1_tiger_fit_ffd.note: distance from modern TIGER road points to nearest Warren ink pixel (capped 15 px at half scale); fitted data, so optimistic; roads also moved since 1863

p2_independent_gcps.note: GCPs were picked by another agent from different features (summits, junctions, buildings) and not used in my fit. A 25 to 30 m median disagreement means either my transform, their GCP picks, or both carry errors of that size; unresolved. Stated positional error of the land-cover polygons is therefore 30 to 40 m, not the 1.4 m of pass 1.

p3_terrain_registration.note: Local best shifts of the Warren sheet (3 km windows, 10 m steps, +-60 m) against slope from 3DEP lidar; windows with NCC>0.28 only; the NCC is weak (peak about 0.3 to 0.47) so this indicates the local error scale (about 20 m), not a correction.

p4_canopy_persistence.note: If the mapped 1863 woods are right, most of their interior should carry canopy today (woods persist); open 1863 ground should carry little. This tests the extraction, not the 1863 truth.

p5_naip_2022_04_leafoff_check.note: April-2022 NAIP is leaf-off/leaf-emerging: woods read lower NDVI than green spring pasture and darker. A clear woods vs open contrast supports the polygons were not drawn on open fields; the exact values are not a pass/fail threshold.
